topics.name: Parts of speech (nouns, pronouns, verbs, word forms)

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Dadaji was sitting near the window.
Dadaji were sitting near the window.
Dadaji was sit near the window.
questions.rule: Past continuous = was/were + -ing. One person takes was: was sitting.
Women is already plural, so add 's: Women's.

options: Riya like posters about brave women.
Riya liking posters about brave women.
Riya likes posters about brave women.
questions.rule: One person (he/she) in the simple present takes -s: Riya likes.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Riya is one person, so use was, not were.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a verb like told, use the object pronoun us, not we.

questions.before: Riya was angry, so Dadaji spoke to
questions.rule: After to, use the object pronoun her.
One person (she) takes is.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the past continuous.
questions.rule: Past continuous: subject + was + verb-ing: Rahul was teasing.

options: We was reading an article about women.
We were read an article about women.
We were reading an article about women.
questions.rule: We takes were, and the past continuous needs the -ing form: were reading.
To show that something belongs to one person, add 's: Meena's poster.

options: Women play an important role in every field.
Women plays an important role in every field.
Women is playing an important role in every field.
questions.rule: Women is plural, so the verb has no -s: women play.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
options: Malala spoke up for girls's education.
Malala spoke up for girls' education.
Malala spoke up for girls education's.
questions.rule: For a plural noun ending in s, add only an apostrophe: girls'.

questions.rule: Riya and her friends = more than one person, so use were making.

questions.rule: The friend belongs to my mother (one person), so write mother's.

questions.before: When Dadaji came in, the children
questions.rule: Came shows the past, and children is plural: were arguing.
One person (she) in the simple present: my grandmother teaches.
Riya's face = the face of Riya. The owner comes first with 's.

options: Yes, she plays cricket every Sunday.
Yes, she play cricket every Sunday.
Yes, she playing cricket every Sunday.
questions.rule: She in the simple present takes -s: she plays.

options: My mother inspires me every day.
My mother inspires I every day.
My mother inspire me every day.
questions.rule: After the verb use the object pronoun me, and my mother takes inspires.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: Rahul was laughing when Riya was grab the paper.
Rahul laughing when Riya grabbed the paper.
Rahul was laughing when Riya grabbed the paper.
questions.rule: The longer action uses was + -ing (was laughing); the short action uses the simple past (grabbed).

options: The childrens' posters were on the art wall.
The children's posters were on the art wall.
The childs' posters were on the art wall.
questions.rule: Children is a plural that does not end in s, so add 's: children's.

questions.rule: The subject is a packet (one), not pens, so use is.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Past continuous = was + -ing: was showing.

questions.after: to every field, from science to sports.
questions.rule: The sentence needs a verb after Women: contribute.
The phone belongs to his uncle, so write uncle's phone.
Past continuous question: What + were + subject + -ing?
She is the subject pronoun; them is the object pronoun after the verb.

chat: I called you at eight last night. You didn't answer.
options: Sorry, I am helping Dadaji with his medicines.
Sorry, I was helping Dadaji with his medicines.
Sorry, I were helping Dadaji with his medicines.
questions.rule: An action going on at a past time (eight last night) takes the past continuous: I was helping.

chat: Who are those women in the photo?
options: They is my teachers from school.
They are my teacher from school.
They are my teachers from school.
questions.rule: They takes are, and more than one person needs the plural teachers.

options: Sarla Thukral was India's first woman pilot.
Sarla Thukral were India's first woman pilot.
Sarla Thukral was India's first woman pilots.
questions.rule: One person takes was, and first ... pilot is singular.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: The girls were practising boxing when it start to rain.
The girls were practising boxing when it started to rain.
The girls was practising boxing when it started to rain.
questions.rule: The girls takes were practising; the sudden action is in the simple past: started.

options: We celebrate Women's Day in 8 March every year.
We celebrates Women's Day on 8 March every year.
We celebrate Women's Day on 8 March every year.
questions.rule: Use on with dates, and we takes celebrate (no -s).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To say how she spoke, use an adverb: spoke angrily.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The dream belongs to Savitribai Phule (one person), so add 's: Phule's dream.
The subject is Riya; along with her friends does not change it. Now needs the present: is.

questions.before: Dadaji was reading the newspaper while the children
questions.rule: Two actions going on at the same past time: was reading ... were playing.
Everyone is singular, so the verb takes -s: deserves.

chat: Did you find your brother's cap?
options: Yes, I founded it under his bed.
Yes, I found it under his bed.
Yes, I find it under he bed.
questions.rule: The past of find is found; it stands for the cap and his shows whose bed.

chat: Why was Riya so upset this morning?
options: Because Rahul was teasing her about an article.
Because Rahul were teasing her about an article.
Because Rahul was tease her about an article.
questions.rule: One person takes was, followed by the -ing form: was teasing.

options: The list of women who showed great courage is very long.
The list of women who showed great courage are very long.
The list of women who shows great courage is very long.
questions.rule: The main subject is the list (one), so is. Who showed refers back to women and is past.

options: Riya's friends were reading the womens' stories aloud.
Riya's friends were reading the women's stories aloud.
Riya's friend's were reading the women's stories aloud.
questions.rule: Women's (plural not ending in s + 's). A simple plural like friends needs no apostrophe.

questions.rule: The subject of the second part is Dadaji (one person), so use was arranging, even though the girls were comes first.

questions.after: names are on the school's list of toppers.
questions.rule: Both means two sisters; for a plural ending in s, add only an apostrophe: sisters'.

questions.after: of International Women's Day to the children.
questions.rule: After the and before of we need a noun: importance.
Past continuous question: Why + was + subject + -ing?
The subject is Kalpana's story (one), so the verb takes -s: inspires.

chat: Who is the woman in your speech?
options: She is my grandmother, and she have taught me to be brave.
She are my grandmother, and she has taught me to be brave.
She is my grandmother, and she has taught me to be brave.
questions.rule: She takes is and has: she has taught.

chat: What were you doing when the power went off?
options: I practising my speech for Women's Day.
I was practising my speech for Women's Day.
I was practise my speech for Women's Day.
questions.rule: The question uses the past continuous, so answer with I was practising.
